about: The Ishtar Gate at Level 1, the last street level, built late in Nebuchadnezzar's reign, after 586 BC, its year unknown. Every number of the gate's scene with its class and source. Classes: M measured in place, R original material placed by inference, T named in the king's text with its form guessed, G guessed; T is shown as G on the switch.

frame.says: origin on the gate's axis in the outer plane of the front gate's front wall (the door's wall), at the +15.40 street; +z out of the face (342.8 true, 343.1 grid), +x to the right of a visitor facing the gate (252.8 true, west), +y up; y 0 is +15.40 in the German excavation zero (25.5 m above sea level)
frame.faceSrc: read off Uppsala sheet 2.28 (Babylon020_IshtarGate, CC BY 4.0) at 600 dpi with GATE-RESEARCH 1.3's pixel formula: the towers' centres stand 2.0 m east of the map's frame origin and the door wall's line 0.8 m south of it; reading plus or minus 0.3 m
frame.mapStreetMasked: the map's street is masked from the main gate's south face to the lion walls' north end; beyond, the map's street and levels stand

units.src: brick about 33 x 33 cm, 10 courses = 86 cm (K1918 p. 16, 19; P2021 p. 34, 71)

street.bearingSrc: street lines north of the gate 13.7 degrees west of grid north on sheet 2.28 (GATE-RESEARCH 1.1)

levels.src: +15.30 at the west connecting wall, where the west postern's stair lands (K1918 p. 11); the postern's place read off sheet 2.28, 8.7 to 12.4 m north of the face
+12.56 beside triangulation point 2 (P2021 p. 228 note 29, from K1918 pl. 35); 99.35 m along the gate's axis from the face, 4.3 m east of it
+7.5 at the North Gate (P2021 p. 228); the stretch beyond point 2 follows the map's line

street.gradeSays: straight grades between the measured spots [Guess between them]; Level 0's later near-level relaying is not shown
street.halfWidthSrc: the lion walls' inner faces read off sheet 2.28 about 18 to 19 m apart north of the bastions (P2021 p. 80: about 20 m); 19 m taken

paving.src: P2021 p. 231 to 232; no wheel ruts (K1914 ch. V)

street.forecourtPaving: breccia with the limestone strip on the axis, as Pedersen's model has it (GATE-RESEARCH 4.3) [Guess]

towers.src: K1918 p. 16; gap read off sheet 2.28

wallTop.src: P2021 p. 78 to 79 (Pedersen's model), GATE-RESEARCH 2.3; the 15 m is the parapet walk at the battlements' foot, the merlons stand 0.6 m above it

towerTop.src: one storey (3 to 4 m) over the walls, K1918 p. 46 to 47

arch.src: semicircular brick arch (K1918 p. 38), crown after P2021 p. 78

guardStorey.src: projecting guard storey with round loopholes (K1918 p. 31, 46); Pedersen draws them rectangular (P2021 p. 50)

court.src: 4 m open to the sky between the buildings (P2021 p. 72, K1918 p. 37)

towers.src: K1918 p. 37; gap read off sheet 2.28

door.src: not stated; 4.5 m like the front gate (GATE-RESEARCH 1.2)

wallTop.src: at least one storey, 3 to 4 m, over the front gate (K1918 p. 47); Pedersén's model 19 m (P2021). Ours 21, accepted by the launcher on 20 Oct: from the street 66 m out on the axis the line over the front gate's merlons passes 0.5 m above a 19 m wall, so at Pedersén's height the main gate hides behind the front gate, and the double gate is the point of the stop; at 21 its battlements show 1.4 m over the front gate's. The desktop camera stays on the axis

towerTop.src: Pedersén's model 22.5 m (GATE-RESEARCH part 8); ours 25, accepted by the launcher on 20 Oct, one storey of 4 m over the 21 m walls, so the main towers' tops show over the front towers from the street on the axis

arch.src: ours: the top of the front door's range, for the larger gate

eastWall.src: 5.50 m plus 3.70 m (K1918 p. 11), inner face read off sheet 2.28

height.src: compared with Pedersen's model (fig. 2.32, late afternoon light, eyes only): the connecting walls stand about half the front gate's walls

wing.src: read off sheet 2.28: the wing between the gate block and the connecting walls, its face 0.45 m behind the gate's face; Nemet-Enlil's outer face 6 m behind the tower fronts (K1918 p. 16)

postern.src: west postern 4.65 m, a stair of 17 steps down west (K1918 p. 12); its place read off sheet 2.28

eastStairs.src: three stairs down on the east side (P2021 p. 73), places read off sheet 2.28

bastions.src: read off sheet 2.28 in the gate's frame, plus or minus 0.5 m; about 21 x 29 m (GATE-RESEARCH 1.2)

height.src: compared with Pedersen's model (fig. 2.32); the map's 12 m

towers.src: towers at their own spacing (K1914 ch. V), read off sheet 2.28: about 7.2 m with 7 m gaps

height.src: compared with Pedersen's street (fig. 2.31, eyes only); the map's 10 m

lions.src: lions about 2 m long, about 60 a side over 180 m, walking north, white with yellow manes or yellow with red manes on light or dark blue (K1914 ch. V; K1918 p. 5); none found in place, so every lion's place is a guess; ground turquoise after the four original panels sampled (COLOURS.md part 4) [Guess]

nemet.src: Nemet-Enlil 3.7 m, mud brick (P2021 p. 59); its outer face 6 m behind the tower fronts (K1918 p. 16)

height.src: raised with the terrain by the gate and perhaps covered (P2021 p. 30); no higher than the front gate's walls; ours

rows.src: animal 13 courses, 11 plain, pitch 24 (K1918 p. 20); rows level (K1918 p. 20); a row one course up across a corner (K1918 p. 19 to 20); 6 rows on the facade and 4 in the door (P2021 p. 78 to 79); the lowest Level 1 row bulls and one colour per row are guesses; row 11 (flat glazed dragons) not shown, Pedersen's reading (P2021 p. 80), Koldewey read it as a base at Level 1 (K1918 p. 52)

bull.src: grid of 9 half bricks (K1918 p. 20, 23, pl. 13)

depth.src: the moulded bodies stand about 4.5 cm over the wall's plane, the manes' locks and curls to about 5.5 cm, read by eye off the open-licence photos of moulded bricks (commons-amin2019-berlin-unglazed-dragon-head-brick and the in-situ rows), never traced; the fields' highest points are printed by fidelity.mjs

corners.src: the borders run up the corner, a red stripe toward it, the corner a blue stripe a quarter brick wide (K1918 p. 22); how they ended at the top is not known (K1918 p. 47)

battlements.src: stepped, blue glazed, steps two courses high with a quarter-brick setback, parapet one or two bricks (K1918 p. 31, 45)

pedestals.src: round, 1.40 m across, 14 m north of the gate (K1918 p. 10, P2021 p. 73 to 74); place read off sheet 2.28
small square pedestal at the east tower's corner (K1918 p. 16), read off sheet 2.28
in the chamber's west half (K1918 p. 16), read off sheet 2.28

bronze.src: 'wild oxen of bronze and raging dragons' at the entrances (East India House inscription col. 6, K1918 p. 53); form, size and facing guessed: plain bronze at the relief animals' proportions

doors.src: door leaves of cedar with copper, bronze thresholds and pivots (K1918 p. 53, col. VI 11 to 18); shown open, their form guessed

roof.src: cedar beams over the chambers (K1918 p. 47); the court open to the sky (K1918 p. 37)

figure.src: the house's grey sign person on the paving by the door (HOUSE-RULES); in front of the east tower, where the floor is in the sun at 17:00 (the west half of the recess lies in the west tower's shadow)

light.about: 17:00 for both stills (the launcher's ruling, 20 Oct). The stack has no GI, so the shade's light is modelled: the map's sky dome, the paving's bounce as the environment's lower half, and the sunlit east walls as a warm band in it. Every value here is ours (G for the method), stated so a reader can redo it.

sun.src: the directional sun in the renderer's units, its colour warming with low elevation (gate.ts setHour). With env 0.6 a lit vertical face gets about three times a shaded one's light, the order of a clear sky at 17 degrees (diffuse about 0.4 of the direct on the ground; textbook order, Ours). At 3.2 with the sky at full strength the lit and shaded faces differed by under 2 to 1 and the hour did not show (HAND/scratch/light, variants a and h)

paving.src: the environment below the horizon: a warm grey scaled by value. Limestone and breccia about 0.6 and 0.3 albedo, 15 percent of the forecourt floor in sun at 17:00 (P1's ray cast), the rest lit by the sky: a dim warm floor, not a bright one

eastWalls.src: the west faces of the east bastion (x -10 to -30, z 21 to 50), the east connecting wall and the east lion wall stand in full sun at 17:00 (light on a west face 0.92). Seen from the door they fill azimuth 10 to 70 degrees east of the face's normal, elevation -2 to 14. Their radiance: albedo 0.35 (buff brick) times the sun on a west face over pi, in the brick's colour; computed per hour in gate.ts

light.envSrc: the environment's strength: the sky dome, the paving's bounce and the east walls' band together; the sky in the picture is the dome itself at full strength
light.exposureSrc: exposed for the lit east tower front: its white dragons near 200 of 255 and the cobalt a clear blue; at 1.0 the cobalt read navy (glaze ground luma 42 on the lit front, HAND/scratch/light). The brighter state is the same picture 0.5 stops up (exposure 1.98), handed in beside it

print.src: a white balance a little warm (a photographer's shade setting), so the shade reads blue-grey and the sun's side warm; saturation 1.1 for new glaze

hour.src: GATE-RESEARCH 5.1 and PILOT/scratch/sun2.py; local apparent solar time, 20 days after the spring equinox
